database.name: Database
database.description: PostgreSQL holds every model, collection, user and setting. Without it nothing in Thingport works.

storage.name: File storage
storage.description: Where model files, their pictures and 3D previews are kept. Uploads, imports and downloads all need it writable, with room to spare.

problems.not_writable: Thingport can't write to its storage folder. Check that the volume is mounted, isn't read-only, and that PUID/PGID match the folder's owner.
problems.low_space: Storage is running low. New uploads and imports will fail once it's full: free up space or give the volume more.

memory.name: Memory

internet.name: Internet

problems.offline: The server can't reach the internet. Check its network, DNS and any proxy or firewall in front of it; Docker containers also need outbound access. Uploading and browsing your library still work.
problems.timeout: Nothing answered in time. The connection may be very slow, or something on the network is dropping requests.

problems.timeout: FlareSolverr didn't answer in time. It may still be starting, or be busy.

storage.heading: Storage Structure
storage.subtitle: Choose how managed model files are organized on disk.
storage.templateDesc: The folders each model's files are saved in, and how the files are named. Every user's files sit in a folder of their own first, so a file ends up at e.g. <user>/Props/Workshop/Cable clip/Cable clip.3mf. Two models can have the same name if they're in different categories, so the path must include Model ID, or both Category or folder and Model name; otherwise their files could land in the same folder. A model's supporting files go beside its model files, and its pictures in an Images folder next to them.

tokens.category-or-folder: The model's category or folder, with parent ones as parent folders
tokens.collection: The collection the model is in. Models in no collection go to "Uncollected", models in several go to "Multiple collections"
tokens.creator: The author shown on the model page; a user's own uploads use their display name
tokens.plate: The file's position in the model, starting at 1

storage.customFolderHint: A fixed name like "Library". It can also mix in tokens such as {model} ({id}).
storage.customFolderSlash: One folder at a time: no "/"
storage.fileNamePlate: Plate number, then file name (1 - Base.3mf)
storage.savedHasProblems: The saved structure was set before these rules. It keeps working, and a new file whose path is taken goes in a folder named after its model's ID instead of replacing another. Pick a structure that follows the rules to save a new one.

problems.empty: Add at least the file name.
problems.stray_brace: There's a { or } that isn't part of a token.
problems.empty_folder: A folder is empty, or named . or ..
problems.filename_count: The file name must be in it exactly once.
problems.filename_not_last: The file name must come last, so each file keeps its extension.
problems.plate_in_folder: The plate number can only be part of the file name; a folder per plate would split a model's files apart.
problems.category_not_whole_folder: Category or folder must be a folder of its own, since it can be several folders deep.

fileReuse.heading: Identical files
fileReuse.subtitle: Save space when several users import the same model.
fileReuse.help: Thingport compares each new model file, supporting file, gallery image and description image with the ones already stored, whichever kind they are. Copy-on-write clones a match on btrfs, XFS or ZFS 2.2 and later, and stores the file as usual elsewhere. Thumbnails and renders aren't shared. Each clone is a file of its own, so editing one on disk never changes another user's. Files stored before it was turned on are checked too, see Existing files.

backfill.label: Existing files
backfill.help: Turning on cloning goes over the files already stored: each one's hash is recorded, then files with the same content are replaced by clones of the oldest one, keeping their own name, place and owner. Only files in Thingport's storage folder are touched, and a file that changes meanwhile is left as it is. Run it again after turning cloning on for a while off, or for files that couldn't be checked. Snapshots of the storage can keep the old copies, so the space freed is an upper bound.

about.grab: Sends your sign-in as you visit pinshape.com.
setup: Install Thingport Grab, enable it on Pinshape and open pinshape.com signed in.
By hand: copy the remember_token cookie of a signed-in pinshape.com tab and paste it in Configuration → Providers.

admin.description: Models, and anyone's collections and likes. Lists read without a sign-in; the files need each user's own.

sync.notConnected: Connect Pinshape in Configuration > Providers, or visit it with Thingport Grab, to see your likes and collections here.

status.alwaysConnected: OwlCAD is connected by default: it needs no account or key.

about.summary: A CAD app that runs in the browser. Its gallery holds a large library of CC0 and CC-BY parts, and the CAD models its users share.
about.grab: Needed for its CAD projects: OwlCAD stores no file for one, so its editor builds it.
setup: Nothing to set up: paste an OwlCAD link, or import from its page with Thingport Grab.
A library part imports straight away. A CAD project waits for Thingport Grab to open it on owlcad.com, where OwlCAD's editor exports it.

admin.description: A browser CAD app: its library parts import on their own, its CAD projects through Thingport Grab.
